about: The strategy of each kind of request a user makes (ADR-0105): how the kind is recognised (`data.signals`, `meta.triggers`, `data.target`, the questions it answers), its plan with the tool of every step, the stages of the Loop it runs (`data.stages`, `data.mode`), where its pieces come from (`data.pieces`), the generators it calls and the facts it cannot start without (`data.needs`).

rows.title: Strategy: a whole system or app (several components)
rows.summary: Never one run: split it into components, one per resource or capability, and run each part with its own strategy, the backend first. The generators write every standard resource; a model writes only the rules and the view details of each part.
body: **The plan.**
1. Inspect: `dragonfly gen inspect` (MCP `project_inspect`). No `config.nuc` yet: `strategy:project` first. Several platforms: one project per platform, the backend first.
2. Limits: every `cannot` and `limit` row whose words the request writes (authentication, payments, push notifications...) is told to the user now, before any code.

3. Decompose (`playbook:decompose-a-spec`): the big parts, one component per resource (a thing it stores or reads) or capability (a thing it does). Write the list: the component, what it holds, what it depends on.
4. Order the parts: a component nobody depends on first; a relation between two entities after both exist.

5. Each part is a run of its own, with its strategy: a stored resource `strategy:resource-db`, a resource of another API `strategy:resource-api`, a rule `strategy:usecase`, a view `strategy:interface`. At most 12 pieces for a model in one run.
6. Between components only the facades: a use case of another component is called through that component's `appcomponent`.
7. The app of the backend comes after it: `strategy:client-of-backend`.
8. At the end, the whole project: `dragonfly build`, `nuclear check .`, `dragonfly test`.
**A model writes:** only each part's own rules and view details; never a standard resource.
**Done when:** every part's run passed, the whole project builds and its tests pass.

**Stop and say it when:** the request does not say which things it stores or what is done with them (ask); which components there are and how they relate is a decision (the user's or the lead's, never a guess); a part needs more than 12 pieces from a model (split it again).
asks: an app for orders with customers, products and payments
quiero todo un sistema de inventario
haz una aplicación completa de reservas
a complete backend for a library

rows.title: Strategy: a new project
rows.summary: A project is made by a command, not written: `dragonfly new <name> -p <platform>`, then its connections and plugins in the two config files, then build, install and test. No model writes anything.
body: **The plan.**
1. `dragonfly new <name> -p backend|mobile|web [-d <dialect>]` (a dialect alone gives its platform).
2. `config.nuc`: the app's name and version, `plugins(...)` for what it uses (the cards `plugin:<platform>.<name>`).
3. `config/project_config.nuc`: the connections (a database, an `Http(baseUrl)`, a model).
4. `dragonfly build`, `dragonfly install`, `dragonfly test`; `dragonfly run` to see it.
5. `dragonfly agent init`, so an AI agent finds the project's rules.
6. The first feature is a request of its own: usually `strategy:resource-db` or `strategy:resource-api`.
**A model writes:** nothing.
**Done when:** `dragonfly test` passes in the new project.
**Stop and say it when:** the machine lacks a tool (`dragonfly doctor` names it); the request names no platform (ask: backend, mobile or web).
asks: how do I scaffold a project

rows.title: Strategy: a whole component (one feature module)
rows.summary: A component is a folder with its facade and whatever it holds: generate it, generate each of its resources, write each rule of its own as a use case and wire it. Other components see only its `appcomponent`.
body: **The plan.**
1. Inspect: `dragonfly gen inspect`; a component of that name that exists makes this `strategy:member` or one of the layer strategies.
2. `dragonfly gen component <component>` (MCP `generate_component`): its facade and its config.
3. Each thing it stores or reads is a resource: `strategy:resource-db` or `strategy:resource-api`, one generator call each.
4. Each rule of its own is `strategy:usecase`: its test first, the use case by a model, `dragonfly gen usecase` to wire it.
5. Mobile and web: each view is `strategy:interface`.
6. What it needs from another component it calls through that component's `appcomponent`, never its use cases or repositories.
7. `nuclear check .` and `dragonfly test`.
**A model writes:** the use cases with rules of their own and the details of the views; never the facade's aliases or a standard resource.
**Done when:** the component's tests pass and `nuclear check .` reports nothing (the architecture rules included).
**Stop and say it when:** the request does not say what the component holds (ask for its resources and its rules).

rows.title: Strategy: a resource that reads another API
rows.summary: One generator call writes all of it from the API's real answer: models (nested ones too), the HTTP repository, a use case per action, the facade, the controller or the list screen. A model writes nothing unless the request adds a rule.
body: **The plan.**
1. Inspect: `dragonfly gen inspect`; the name must not be declared already.
2. The shape: `api_inspect <url>` shows the real answer (keys, types, nested objects, a page). `--from-json <url>` reads it by itself.
3. Dry run first: `dragonfly gen resource <component> <Name> --from-json <url> --actions list,get[,search] --dry-run`; on mobile and web add `--screen <screen>` for its list.
4. Run it without `--dry-run`. A snake_case key gets `@key`; a nested object becomes `<Name><Key>`; a paged answer `<Name>Page`.
5. Neither the request nor the API gives the fields: look up the API's documentation (`web_search`, `web_read`); still unclear: ask, never guess.
6. A rule on top of it (a filter, a transformation) is `strategy:usecase`.
7. `nuclear check .`, `dragonfly test` (mobile and web: the generated test mocks the repository; backend: the tester writes one, the generator has none yet).
**A model writes:** nothing; only a use case when the request states a rule of its own.
**Done when:** the generated files compile, the generated tests pass and the route or the screen answers the API's data.
**Stop and say it when:** the url does not answer JSON or needs a key the request does not give (ask); the API is not public (`web_read` refuses local addresses).
asks: list the characters of this API
consume the Rick and Morty API
lista los personajes de esta API
trae los datos de una API externa
un recurso que lee otra API

needs.url: Which url answers it? Give a `GET <url>` line, or an example of its answer.

rows.title: Strategy: a resource stored in the database (backend CRUD)
rows.summary: One generator call writes the entity, the `New<Name>` model, the paged repository, a use case per action, the facade, the controller and the tests. A model writes only a relation to another entity or a rule of its own.
body: **The plan.**
1. Inspect: `dragonfly gen inspect`; the name must not be declared already (it is: `strategy:member`).
2. The fields: the request's `Key | Type` table or example (`--from-spec <spec.md>`), or `--fields "id:int total:double status:string"`. No fields: ask.
3. Dry run: `dragonfly gen resource <component> <Name> --source db [--actions list,get,create,update,delete] --dry-run`, then for real.
4. A relation to another entity is one piece for a model: the entity's file with the relation's decorator (the card of `kind:backend.entity`); the generator writes none yet.
5. The database already has tables: `strategy:data-migration` (`dragonfly migrate make "<message>"`).
6. A rule (an order is cancelled only when pending) is `strategy:usecase`.
7. `nuclear check .`, `dragonfly test`: the generated tests add a row and find it, and ask for a missing one.
**A model writes:** nothing; a relation between entities and each rule of its own.
**Done when:** the generated tests pass and every route answers.

**Stop and say it when:** the request gives no fields (ask); a field's type is a model nobody declares (declare it first, or it stops); the project has no database connection (`strategy:configuration`).
asks: guarda los pedidos en la base de datos
store the readers with name and email

needs.fields: Which fields does it have, and of which type? Give a `Key | Type` table, an example answer, the API's url or `name:type` pairs.

rows.title: Strategy: the app of a Dragonfly backend (its contract)
rows.summary: The backend's contract writes the app's models and repositories; a use case per action is one generator call each; only the screens are left, each with `strategy:interface`.
body: **The plan.**
1. `contracts(<name> = "<path or url of the backend>")` in `config.nuc` (one piece: that file).
2. `nuclear contracts update`: `contracts/<name>/` gets a model per backend model and a repository per controller, already compiling.
3. A use case per action: `dragonfly gen usecase <component> <Name> --calls <Contract>Repository.<method>`.
4. Each screen: `strategy:interface` (a list of a resource is `dragonfly gen resource ... --screen`).
5. `nuclear check .`: N0116 on a contract member means the backend changed (`nuclear contracts update` again).
**A model writes:** only the details of the views.
**Done when:** the app builds against the contract and its tests pass.
**Stop and say it when:** the backend is not a Dragonfly project (it has no contract: `strategy:resource-api` from its answers instead).
asks: build the mobile app for this backend
consume our backend from the web app

rows.title: Strategy: only an interface: a screen or a view (mobile, web)
rows.summary: A resource's list is one generator call. Any other screen is three small files written in order: the state model, the state manager, the view. The view calls only its manager, the manager only the facade.
body: **The plan.**
1. Inspect: `dragonfly gen inspect`; the use case the screen needs must exist in the component's facade (it does not: `strategy:usecase` first).
2. A list of a resource: `dragonfly gen resource <component> <Name> ... --screen <screen>` and it is done.
3. Another view: `dragonfly make screen <component> <screen> --route /<path>` leaves the three files in `presentation/<screen>/`.
4. Piece 1, the state model: one line with its states (`loaded`, `error`, `loading`), with the card of its kind and the pitfall `pitfall:state-model-shape`.
5. Piece 2, the state manager: `@stateModel(State)`, each method marked with the state it emits, calling the facade (`pitfall:state-manager-shape`).
6. Piece 3, the view: `@screen(route, providers)` over a `stateless`; it draws with `<State>Builder`, one callback per state.
7. Tests first: `@states(...)` for the manager, `@widget(...)` for the view.
8. `nuclear check .` (N0301: a view that calls a repository or a use case) and `dragonfly test`.
**A model writes:** the three pieces, one file each, in that order; examples of the same kind only.
**Done when:** the screen's tests pass and the architecture check is clean.

**Stop and say it when:** the project is a backend (it has no screens: say so); the request does not say what the screen shows or which states it has (ask); a form or a translation on web (`limit:web-first-version`).
asks: just the UI for the cart
una pantalla que muestre el pedido

rows.title: Strategy: only a repository, or a query in one
rows.summary: A repository of a new model is a resource (the generator writes both). A new method in a repository the project has is one piece: that file. To let the rest of the app call it, `dragonfly gen usecase --calls` writes its use case and wires it.
body: **The plan.**
1. Inspect: `dragonfly gen inspect`; read the repository and its model (the project's files).
2. The model does not exist: this is a resource, `strategy:resource-api` or `strategy:resource-db`.

3. A new method or query: one piece, the repository's own file, with the card of `kind:<platform>.repository` and its pitfalls (backend: `pitfall:query-operators-are-functions`; mobile: `pitfall:mobile-repository-request`).
4. `nuclear check .`.
5. Expose it: `dragonfly gen usecase <component> <Name> --calls <Repository>.<method>` and, on the backend, `--route "GET <prefix>/<path>"`.
6. `dragonfly test`: a test for the new query (backend: rows created before they are read).
**A model writes:** the one method, in the file that already exists.
**Done when:** the project compiles, the new use case is in the facade and its test passes.
**Stop and say it when:** the request does not say what the query filters or returns (ask).

rows.title: Strategy: a use case: one rule of the business
rows.summary: A use case that only calls a repository is one generator call. One with a rule of its own is a test first, then one file by a model, then `dragonfly gen usecase` wires it: its alias in the facade and, on the backend, its route.
body: **The plan.**
1. Inspect: `dragonfly gen inspect`; the repository and the models it uses must exist (they do not: a resource strategy first).
2. It only calls a repository method: `dragonfly gen usecase <component> <Name> --calls <Repository>.<method> [--route "<VERB> <prefix>/<path>"]` and it is done.
3. It has a rule: the test first, one `@test` per acceptance criterion (the normal case, each error).
4. One piece for a model: `components/<component>/domain/usecases/<name>.nuc`, one `exec(...) Result<Error, T>`, with the card of `kind:<platform>.usecase` and `pitfall:one-exec-per-use-case`.
5. Wire it: `dragonfly gen usecase <component> <Name> [--route "POST orders/{id}/cancel"]`. The signature is read from the project; a `{name}` of the path is a parameter of `exec`.
6. Mobile and web: what a screen shows of it is `strategy:interface`.
7. `nuclear check .`, `dragonfly test`.
**A model writes:** the use case with its rule, one file; never its alias or its route.
**Done when:** its tests pass, its alias is in the facade and (backend) its route answers.
**Stop and say it when:** the rule is not stated (ask for it: what is allowed, what is refused and with which error); the generator refuses (`failure:the-generator-refuses` says what is missing).
asks: cancel an order only when it is pending
un caso de uso que cancele el pedido
add a use case that lists the books of an author
agrega una regla: no se puede pagar dos veces

rows.title: Strategy: a route of the API (backend)
rows.summary: A route is never written by hand: `dragonfly gen usecase <component> <Name> --route "<VERB> <prefix>/<path>"` adds it to the controller of its prefix, calling the use case. No use case yet: that one first.
body: **The plan.**
1. Inspect: `dragonfly gen inspect`: which use case answers the route.
2. The use case exists: `dragonfly gen usecase <component> <Name> --route "<VERB> <prefix>/<path>" --dry-run`, then for real. The controller of the prefix is made when missing.
3. It does not: `strategy:usecase` first (`--calls` when it only calls a repository).
4. A `{name}` of the path must be a parameter of the use case; the other parameters arrive as the verb sends them.
5. A fixed segment wins over a parameter (`orders/pending` before `orders/{id}`): nothing to order by hand.
6. `nuclear check .`, `dragonfly test`, and the route over HTTP when the app runs.
**A model writes:** nothing; a controller never holds logic.
**Done when:** the route answers what the use case answers, with its status.
**Stop and say it when:** the route's verb or path is not given (ask); the project is not a backend (mobile and web have no routes).
asks: expose this use case over HTTP
a new route for the report

rows.title: Strategy: one declaration: a model, an entity, a service, a listener...
rows.summary: `dragonfly make <kind> <component> <Name>` puts the file in its folder with its shape; a model fills it in, with the card of its kind and the mistakes small models repeat with it; the compiler checks it.
body: **The plan.**
1. Inspect: `dragonfly gen inspect`; the name must be new (it exists: `strategy:member`).
2. The kind: the word the request writes (how people say each kind comes from the kinds' cards: "application component" is `appcomponent`).
3. A model with its repository and actions is a resource: a resource strategy, not this one.
4. `dragonfly make <kind> <component> <Name>`: the file where the platform's layout puts it.
5. One piece for a model: that file, with `kind:<platform>.<kind>`, every pitfall of the kind and examples of the same kind only.
6. `nuclear check`; the compiler's errors come with their cards, three repairs at most.
7. It has logic (a service, a converter, a guard): one test.
**A model writes:** the one file.
**Done when:** the file compiles in the project and, when it has logic, its test passes.
**Stop and say it when:** the request does not give its fields or signatures (ask); the kind is not of the project's platform (`nuclear help words --platform <platform>` lists them).

un modelo Lector con nombre y correo
add a service that computes the total
a listener for the order created event

rows.title: Strategy: one more thing in what exists: a field, a method, an action
rows.summary: Read the declaration and who uses it, change the file that declares it, and let the compiler name every other file that must follow. A new action of a resource is a generator call; a field of an entity ends with a migration.
body: **The plan.**
1. Read: the outline of the declaring file and who writes the name (the project's files: `outline`, `grep`).

2. A new action of a resource (search, delete...): `dragonfly gen resource <component> <Name> --actions <new> --dry-run`, then for real: it adds the use case, the facade's alias, the repository's method and the route, and keeps the rest.
3. A field: one piece per file that declares it. The entity or the model; on the backend also `New<Name>`, which the create and update use cases copy from.
4. A method: one piece, the declaring file; a use case gets no second method (`pitfall:one-exec-per-use-case`): that is a new use case, `strategy:usecase`.
5. `nuclear check .` names each file that must follow (a test that builds the model, a use case that copies its fields): one repair per file.
6. An entity changed and the database exists: `strategy:data-migration`. The backend's contract changed: `nuclear contracts update` in its apps.
7. `dragonfly test`; a test for what was added.
**A model writes:** the changed file, whole, with the file as it is in front of it.
**Done when:** the project compiles, the old tests pass and a new test covers what was added.
**Stop and say it when:** the request does not give the field's type or the method's signature (ask); the name is not in the project (it is new: `strategy:declaration`).
asks: add a note field to Order
agrega el campo nota a Order
agrega la acción de buscar a los libros

needs.declaration: Which declaration is it? Write its name as the project declares it (`Order`, `CancelOrder`): `dragonfly gen inspect` lists them.

rows.title: Strategy: a rename
rows.summary: A tool does it, no model: every file that writes the old name as a word is written again with the new one, the compiler checks them together and the tests pass before and after. No test is deleted.
body: **The plan.**
1. `dragonfly test`: what passes now must pass at the end. Red before starting: fix that first (`strategy:bug-failing-test`).
2. The name must be a declaration of the project (`Book`, `CancelOrder`): a field or a method is renamed by hand, and the compiler then names every use.

3. The names: the old one and every declaration of the project built from it by a word before or after (`NewBook`, `BookRepository`, `CreateBook` for `Book`). They follow it because the platform binds some of them to it by name: a repository `BookRepository` is the repository of `Book`. A plural (`ListBooks`) and an alias of the facade (`createBook()`) are other names and stay. The analysis lists every name it changes.

4. The files: the project's files tool (`renamed`) answers every `.nuc` that writes one of those names as a word, each whole with the new names; the facade and the tests are among them. They are the run's pieces, written as they are.
5. No security review: a rename writes no new logic.
6. `nuclear check .`: a use the tool could not see (a name built from another, a text) is an error with its line, repaired like any compiler error.
7. The declaring file keeps its path: move it by hand when its name should follow (no tool moves a file yet).
8. `dragonfly test`.
**A model writes:** nothing; only the repair of an error the compiler finds afterwards.
**Done when:** `nuclear check .` reports nothing, every test that passed still passes and the old name is written nowhere.
**Stop and say it when:** the old name is not in the project; the new name is declared already; the name is of the platform or a library (it cannot change).
asks: change the name of CancelOrder to RevokeOrder
rename the field total to amount

needs.names: Which name changes, and to what? Write `rename <Old> to <New>`.

rows.title: Strategy: a refactor that moves, extracts, splits or merges
rows.summary: Where to cut needs several files understood at once: a frontier model or the user decides it and writes the pieces; the local agents do each mechanical step, one file at a time, the compiler after each and the tests before and after.
body: **The plan.**
1. `dragonfly test`: green before anything moves.
2. The lead reads the files (`project_inspect`, the project map `.nuclear/map.md`) and decides the cut: what moves where, what the new declaration is called and declares.
3. The new declaration first: `dragonfly make <kind> <component> <Name>` and one piece (`strategy:declaration`).
4. Each file that uses what moved: one piece, with the file as it is and the exact change.
5. A use case that moves to another component: `dragonfly gen usecase` adds its alias there; the old alias is removed by hand.
6. `nuclear check .` after every piece (the architecture rules N03xx say what a move broke), `nuclear fix .` for the exact fixes.
7. `dragonfly test`: no test deleted, none weakened.
**A model writes:** each mechanical step the lead wrote; never the decision of where to cut.
**Done when:** the same tests pass and the architecture check is clean.
**Stop and say it when:** no frontier model leads and the request does not list the exact steps (`limit:agent-reasoning`: say it and ask for the steps or for a lead).
asks: extract this rule into a service
extrae esa regla a un servicio
move the use case to the orders component
divide este caso de uso en dos
refactor the checkout without changing behaviour

rows.title: Strategy: a break of the architecture's rules
rows.summary: The compiler names every break (N03xx) with the rule and the line. Almost every one is fixed the same way: the alias goes into the facade with `dragonfly gen usecase`, and the caller calls the facade.
body: **The plan.**
1. `nuclear check .`: each N03xx with its file, line and rule.
2. The card of each code (`error:N0301`...): what the rule protects and how it is fixed.
3. A use case called from outside its component: `dragonfly gen usecase <component> <Name>` puts its alias in the facade; the caller's file is one piece: call the `appcomponent`.
4. A view that calls a repository or a use case: the call moves into its state manager, which calls the facade (two pieces).
5. A file in the wrong folder: `nuclear help layout --platform <platform>` gives the folder of its kind; moved by hand.
6. `nuclear check .` again, then `dragonfly test`.
**A model writes:** each file that breaks a rule, with the exact call to make.
**Done when:** `nuclear check .` reports no N03xx and the tests pass.
**Stop and say it when:** fixing a break needs a new boundary between components (a decision: the lead or the user).
asks: the view calls the repository directly
a use case is used from another component

rows.title: Strategy: a change of the database's schema (backend)
rows.summary: Change the entity, let the tool write the migration from the difference, read what it drops, apply it. The migration is generated, never written by hand.
body: **The plan.**
1. The entity: `strategy:member` (the field, its type, its `@column` options) or a relation's decorator.
2. `nuclear check .`.
3. `dragonfly migrate make "<message>"`: the migration comes from the difference between the entities and the last one.
4. Read it: it warns about a column or a table it drops. Data would be lost: stop and ask.
5. A column that is not null on a table with rows needs a default (`@column(default = ...)`).
6. `dragonfly migrate` applies it; `dragonfly migrate down` takes it back.
7. `dragonfly test`.
**A model writes:** the entity's file.
**Done when:** the migration applies on a database with data, the tests pass, and `dragonfly migrate make` again says there is nothing to change.
**Stop and say it when:** the migration drops data; the database is not SQLite and was never tried (`limit:untested`: say it).
asks: add an index to the email
cambia el tipo de la columna

needs.declaration: Which declaration is it? Write its name as the project declares it (`Order`, `CancelOrder`): `dragonfly gen inspect` lists them.

rows.title: Strategy: the project's configuration: a connection, a plugin, the app's data
rows.summary: Two files hold it: `config.nuc` (the app, its plugins, its contracts, its dependencies) and `config/project_config.nuc` (the connections). One piece each, then build and install, because the packages change.
body: **The plan.**
1. Which file: a plugin, the app's name or version, a contract or a dependency is `config.nuc`; a database, an `Http(baseUrl)`, a broker or a model is `config/project_config.nuc`.
2. The cards: `plugin:<platform>.<name>` for what a plugin brings and needs, `platform:<platform>` for the connections it has.
3. One piece: that file, with the file as it is.
4. `nuclear check .`: N0303 for a wrong manifest, N0304 for a kind of a plugin that is off, N0305 for one the platform lacks.
5. `dragonfly build` and `dragonfly install`: the target's packages follow the plugins.
6. `dragonfly test`.
**A model writes:** the one config file.
**Done when:** the project builds, installs and its tests pass.
**Stop and say it when:** a secret is asked to be written in the file (never: it goes in the environment); the service was never run for real (`limit:untested`).
asks: configura la conexión a la API

rows.title: Strategy: taking something out
rows.summary: Find who uses it, take the uses out first and the declaration last, the compiler after each step. The Loop writes files and never deletes one: the deletion itself is done by the lead or by hand.
body: **The plan.**
1. Who uses it: every file that writes the name (the project's files: `grep`), its alias in the facade, its route, its tests.
2. The uses first: one piece per file that calls it (the call and what depended on it taken out).
3. The alias and the route: the lines of the facade and the controller, by hand or by the lead.
4. The declaration's file and its tests: deleted by hand (`git rm`).
5. `nuclear check .` after each step; `dragonfly test`.
6. An entity removed: `strategy:data-migration`, and it drops a table: ask first.
**A model writes:** the files that used it, each without the use.
**Done when:** the name is written nowhere, the project compiles and the remaining tests pass.
**Stop and say it when:** data would be dropped; something outside the project uses it (a client of the contract).

signals: \b(ya no (usamos|se usa|hace falta)|no longer (used|needed)|we no longer use)\b

rows.title: Strategy: the project does not compile
rows.summary: No planning and no new tests: the compiler's exact fixes first (`nuclear fix .`), then each file that still has errors is repaired with the card of each error (three attempts, each checked by the compiler); what is left goes to the lead.
body: **The plan.**
1. `nuclear check . --json`: every error with its code, file, line and, for most, its fix.
2. `nuclear fix .` applies every exact fix: a tool does what needs no thinking.
3. What is left, by file: the card of each code (`error:N0xxx`, with the errors it comes with) and the mistakes small models repeat (the pitfalls of the file's kind).
4. One repair per file: the file as it is, its errors and their cards. Never a change in `build/`.
5. `nuclear check .` again. What is still wrong after its file was repaired goes to the lead, with the errors and what was tried.
6. `dragonfly test`: a fix must not turn a test red.
**A model writes:** each file that has errors, repaired.
**Done when:** `nuclear check .` reports nothing and the tests that passed still pass.

**Stop and say it when:** the repair did not clear it (the lead takes the file, with the errors and what was tried); the error is in a generated or installed file (`failure:the-installed-tools-are-old`, `dragonfly doctor`).

rows.title: Strategy: a test fails
rows.summary: Run it, read the failure in Nuclear (`dragonfly explain`), decide which is wrong, the test or the code, by the acceptance criterion, repair that one file and run again. A test is never deleted or weakened to pass.
body: **The plan.**
1. `dragonfly test`: which test, which message.
2. `dragonfly explain`: the failure told in Nuclear, the `.nuc` file and line, a hint.
3. Which is wrong: the criterion decides. The test asks for what the criterion says: the code is wrong. It asks for something else: the test is.
4. The usual causes: `pitfall:test-reads-an-empty-database` (rows are created before they are read), `pitfall:result-read-as-its-value`, `pitfall:a-call-without-its-await`.

5. One repair: the file of the code the failure names, with the failure as `dragonfly explain` tells it. A failure that names only the test stops here: a test is not rewritten to pass, and where the cause is needs the lead or the user.
6. `dragonfly test` again; three rounds.
7. It passes: every other test still passes.
**A model writes:** the one file that is wrong.
**Done when:** the test passes, no other test turned red, and no assertion was removed.
**Stop and say it when:** the test and the criterion disagree and the request does not say which holds (ask); the failure is not of the code (`strategy:bug-environment`).

signals: \b(test|tests|prueba|pruebas)\b.{0,50}\b(dej[oó] de pasar|dejaron de pasar|stopped passing|no longer pass(es)?|does not pass|doesn't pass|no pasa|no pasan)\b

rows.title: Strategy: it does the wrong thing (no test shows it yet)
rows.summary: Reproduce it first: the smallest test that fails for the reason the user gives. From there it is a failing test, and the new test stays.
body: **The plan.**
1. What should happen and what happens: both from the request. One is missing: ask.
2. Reproduce: one `@test` that states what should happen (the tester, from that sentence and the project map). It must fail now.
3. It passes: the bug is not where the request says; say it and ask where it was seen.
4. `dragonfly explain` of the failure: the `.nuc` file and line.

5. Search the errors shelf with the behaviour: many bugs are a habit of another language (`pitfall:library-names-of-other-languages`, `pitfall:replace-changes-only-the-first`, `pitfall:result-read-as-its-value`).
6. The request names the declaration (`CancelOrder`): its file is the piece, with the request as its task. It names none: the failure's own frames say the file.
7. Find every caller of what changes (the project's files) and fix it once, where it starts.
8. `dragonfly test`: the new test and every old one.
**A model writes:** the reproducing test, then the one file with the cause.
**Done when:** the new test passes, every old test passes, and two lines say the cause and the fix.
**Stop and say it when:** the bug cannot be reproduced with a test (a real device, a real service: `limit:untested`); the fix needs a decision about what the right behaviour is (ask).

there is a bug in the cancel flow
no funciona el filtro por autor

signals: \b(should|must|deber[ií]a|debe)\b.{0,90}\b(but|pero|instead|en vez|en lugar|and it|y da|y devuelve|y responde)\b
\b(no funciona|doesn't work|does not work|not working|sale mal|est[aá] mal)\b
\b[1-5]\d\d\b.{0,40}\b(instead of|en vez de|en lugar de|should be|deber[ií]a ser)\b

needs.expected: What should happen, and what happens instead? One sentence each.

rows.title: Strategy: it fails while running: an exception, a crash, a 500
rows.summary: The trace is of the generated code: `dragonfly explain` turns it into the `.nuc` file and line. A test reproduces it, then it is a failing test.
body: **The plan.**
1. The trace or the log: from the request. None: `dragonfly test` or `dragonfly run` to get one, or ask.
2. `dragonfly explain`: the `.nuc` file and line of each frame, and a hint. Never read or fix `build/`.
3. The errors shelf with the message: a failure of a tool (`failure:*`) or a mistake of the code (`pitfall:a-call-without-its-await`, `pitfall:result-read-as-its-value`, `limit:untyped-values`).
4. A test that reproduces it (the tester): it fails with the same message.
5. One repair: the file `dragonfly explain` named.
6. `dragonfly test`; then the same call again when the app runs.
**A model writes:** the reproducing test and the one file.
**Done when:** the test passes and the call no longer fails.
**Stop and say it when:** the failure is of the machine or a service, not of the code (`strategy:bug-environment`); it only happens on a real device or a real database (`limit:untested`).

needs.where: Where does it fail? Paste the message, the output of the command or the test's name.

rows.title: Strategy: the data does not match: a field is empty, renamed or of another type
rows.summary: Compare the real answer with the model: `api_inspect` shows the shape, the model says what was expected. The fix is in the model (`@key`, an optional `?`, a type); with a contract, `nuclear contracts update`.
body: **The plan.**
1. The real shape: `api_inspect <url>` (keys, types, what is null).
2. The model: its file (the project's files). Line by line against the shape: a key written another way, a value that can be null, a type that changed.
3. A snake_case or renamed key: `@key("<key>")` on the field. A value that may be missing: `?` on its type. Another type: the field's type.
4. Easier for many fields: `dragonfly gen resource ... --from-json <url> --dry-run` shows the model the answer gives now; copy the difference.
5. A backend of the project changed: `nuclear contracts update` in the app; N0116 names each use of a member that is gone.
6. A 400 or 422 on a POST: the body against the backend's model and its rules (`failure:a-request-is-invalid`).
7. A test with the real answer as its example; `dragonfly test`.
**A model writes:** the model's file.
**Done when:** the model reads the real answer and a test holds an example of it.
**Stop and say it when:** the API needs a key or is not reachable (ask for an example answer).

needs.declaration: Which declaration is it? Write its name as the project declares it (`Order`, `CancelOrder`): `dragonfly gen inspect` lists them.

rows.title: Strategy: a screen shows the wrong thing (mobile, web)
rows.summary: A screen shows a state: reproduce the wrong one with a `@states` test of its state manager, fix the manager (or the view's builder for that state), then the `@widget` test.
body: **The plan.**
1. Which screen, which state: from the request (it stays loading, the list is empty, the error is not shown).
2. Read its three files: the state model, the state manager, the view.
3. A `@states(...)` test of the manager: the states it must emit for that case, in order. It fails now.
4. The usual causes: a method that never emits its last state, a `Result` read as its value, a call without its await, a state the view has no callback for.
5. One repair: the manager, or the view's builder.
6. The `@widget(...)` test of the view; `dragonfly test`.
7. `nuclear check .`: N0301 when the fix made the view call past its manager.
**A model writes:** the reproducing test and the one file.
**Done when:** the manager emits the right states and the view's test passes.
**Stop and say it when:** it is seen only on a real device or browser (`limit:untested`); it is a matter of looks, which no test shows (the user checks it on a device).

rows.title: Strategy: the machine or a service fails, not the code
rows.summary: Nothing of the project changes. Name the failure (the failures of the errors shelf), run `dragonfly doctor`, do what the failure's card says, and try again.
body: **The plan.**
1. The message: from the request or the failed step's log.
2. The local diagnoser classifies it: passing (a service that was down), environment (something missing on the machine), or the code after all.

3. The failure's card: `failure:the-developer-is-not-running`, `failure:the-graph-is-not-running`, `failure:a-model-is-missing`, `failure:a-package-is-missing`, `failure:a-command-is-not-found`, `failure:the-disk-is-full`, `failure:a-call-timed-out`.
4. `dragonfly doctor`: what of the machine is missing; `dragonfly install` for the project's packages.
5. Do what the card says, then run the failed step again (`nuclear-loop retry`).
6. It was the code after all: `strategy:bug-runtime` or `strategy:bug-compile`.
**A model writes:** nothing.
**Done when:** the step that failed passes with no file of the project changed.
**Stop and say it when:** the fix needs something only the user can do (install a system package, free the disk, start a service with their account).

rows.title: Strategy: tests for what exists
rows.summary: One file of tests per declaration, one `@test` per behaviour: the normal case, the edges, each error. Only names the project has. A new test that fails may have found a bug: it is reported, never bent to pass.
body: **The plan.**
1. What to test: the declarations the request names (the project map `.nuclear/map.md` gives their members).
2. For each: its behaviours, from its code and the acceptance criteria.

3. The tester writes `test/<name>_test.nuc` (`tests <Name>`), with examples of the `tests` kind of the same platform and its pitfalls (`pitfall:test-injects-an-unknown-class`, `pitfall:test-reads-an-empty-database`).
4. Backend: the database is in memory and empty in each test. Mobile and web: `@mock` for the repository, `@states` for a manager, `@widget` for a view.
5. `nuclear check .`, `dragonfly test`.
6. A new test fails: `dragonfly explain`. The code is wrong: say it (`strategy:bug-behaviour`); the test is: repair the test.
**A model writes:** the test files.
**Done when:** the new tests compile and pass, or a failing one is reported as a bug with its message.
**Stop and say it when:** the request names something the project does not declare; a backend resource over another API has no mock yet (`limit:generators`).

rows.title: Strategy: a security review
rows.summary: The local reviewer reads each file against the platform's security rules and the project's security commands run. A critical finding stops the run; nothing is changed without saying it.
body: **The plan.**
1. Which files: the ones the request names, or every file changed in the run.
2. The security rules of the platform (`skill:security`): what a route may answer, what is validated, where a secret may be.
3. The local reviewer, one file at a time: each finding with its line and how grave it is.
4. The project's security commands (`.nuclear/loop.json`).
5. A critical finding: it is fixed as `strategy:bug-behaviour` (a test that shows it, then the fix).
6. What the platform cannot do yet (guards on routes, sessions) is said, not worked around (`limit:backend-not-yet`).
**A model writes:** nothing; it reviews.
**Done when:** every file was read and each finding is listed with its line.
**Stop and say it when:** the review needs to understand the whole app's flow of data (a frontier model's review).

rows.title: Strategy: documentation of what was built
rows.summary: The local agents read and write only Nuclear: they answer the text (what each declaration does, from the project map and the code) and write doc comments in `.nuc`; a `.md` file is put in place by the user or the lead.
body: **The plan.**
1. What to document: the declarations or the component the request names (the project map `.nuclear/map.md`).
2. A doc comment (`//` lines above a declaration): one piece per file, the file as it is, the comments added and nothing else changed. The map and the editor show them.

3. A text for people (a README section, how to use the API): the assistant or the documenter answers it from the map and the code; the contract and the OpenAPI document (`.nuclear/openapi.json`) are already generated.
4. Every run of the Loop is documented by itself: its journal says what was built, how it was checked and what is left.
5. A diagram: the lead draws it (`graph_prompt("diagram")`).
**A model writes:** doc comments in `.nuc`; the text of the answer.
**Done when:** the comments compile (`nuclear check .`) and the text names only what the project has.
**Stop and say it when:** a document in another format is asked to be written to disk (`limit:agent-nuclear-only`: the lead or the user).

rows.title: Strategy: a question: explain, do not change
rows.summary: No run and no file: the assistant answers from the graph's cards, the project map and the files the question names, in the language it was asked.
body: **The plan.**
1. The cards closest to the question, over every shelf (what it is, how it is done, what can and cannot be done).
2. The project: its map, and the files that declare the names the question writes.
3. The answer names the command, the kind or the row; code it shows is Nuclear.
4. The graph does not know: it says so; a fact about an outside API is looked up (`web_search`, a frontier model's tool).
5. The question hides an order ("can you add..."): it says which strategy the order is, and that `/task` or a spec runs it.
**A model writes:** nothing.
**Done when:** the question is answered with what the graph and the project say, or it says it does not know.
**Stop and say it when:** the answer would need a decision or a change: that is an order, not a question.

rows.title: Strategy: building, running, migrating, shipping
rows.summary: Commands, not code: the project's own pipeline in `.nuclear/loop.json` (check, test, security, artifacts, deploy), the same ones the exported CI runs. No model writes anything.
body: **The plan.**
1. Which command: build (`dragonfly build`), install, run, test, migrate (`dragonfly migrate`), the deploy of `.nuclear/loop.json`.
2. Before shipping: `nuclear check .` and `dragonfly test`.
3. The artifacts: the build's output, the contract and the OpenAPI document, kept with the run.
4. Deploy: the `seed`, `integration` and `deploy` commands of `.nuclear/loop.json`; `nuclear-loop export` writes the same pipeline for GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket.
5. A command fails: the diagnoser says whether it was passing, the environment or the code; then `strategy:bug-environment` or a bug strategy.
**A model writes:** nothing.
**Done when:** every command of the pipeline exited 0.
**Stop and say it when:** a command is not declared in `.nuclear/loop.json` (the Loop runs only declared commands: add it there first); the target was never run for real (`limit:untested`).

rows.title: Strategy: something NuclearLang or the local agents cannot do
rows.summary: Say it before writing anything: the row that names the limit, what is possible instead, and who takes it (a frontier model, the user, a later version). Never half of it.
body: **The plan.**
1. Which limit: the capabilities rows whose words the request writes (`cannot:*`, `limit:*`).
2. By design: target code is never read or converted into Nuclear (`cannot:read-target-code`); Node.js with Express is postponed (`cannot:nodejs-express`).
3. Not yet in a platform: `limit:backend-not-yet`, `limit:mobile-not-yet`, `limit:web-first-version`, `limit:generators`.

4. Beyond a local model, not the platform: one small file per order, 8192 tokens, no judgment (`limit:agent-one-file`, `limit:agent-context`, `limit:agent-reasoning`): a frontier model leads (`playbook:escalate`).
5. What is possible instead: the closest thing the platform does, with its row.
6. The part of the request that is possible is a request of its own, with its strategy.
**A model writes:** nothing.
**Done when:** the user knows what cannot be done, why, and what can.
**Stop and say it when:** always: this strategy is the stop.
